body.translated_text: <s>Mṛtyuvañcanasitatārāsādhana</s> (The Sādhana of <s>Sitatārā</s> [White Tārā] for Cheating Death)

children.translated_text: One who meditates on the heart-<s>cakra</s> of <s>Tārā</s> becomes untouched by the faults of death,

children.text: lābhī ca sarvasiddhīnāṃ ṣaṇmāsāvadhi tatparaḥ // Mvsts_1 //
children.translated_text: and attains all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments) within six months, being devoted to that [practice]. (1)
From the collection on cheating death based on the instructions composed by <s>Vāgīśvara</s> (Lord of Speech),
the meditation on <s>Sitatārā</s> (White Tārā) that destroys fear is extracted. (2)
Having seen [the deity] shining in the sky with the radiance of the letter 'ta' — the first of the fourth group —

children.text: sitābjendvāsanāṃ dṛṣṭvā puras triśaraṇaṃ paṭhet // Mvsts_3 //
children.translated_text: seated on a white lotus and moon, one should recite the Triple Refuge before [her]. (3)
For a moment one should contemplate <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), for the removal of ordinary [appearances];
then, by the power of aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>), the syllable of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind) should arise. (4)
Upon a moon-disc seat in the center of a white lotus,
[one should visualize her] seated in <s>vajraparyaṅka</s> (diamond cross-legged posture), holding a boon-granting <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), (5)
having the appearance of autumn moonbeams, supported by a moon at her back,
adorned with all ornaments, having the body of a sixteen-year-old, (6)
the mother of all Perfectly Awakened Ones and their sons, who assumes forms at will —

children.text: dhyātvāryatārāṃ hṛdaye tasyāś cakraṃ sitadyuti // Mvsts_7 //
children.translated_text: having meditated on Noble <s>Tārā</s>, [one should visualize] at her heart a <s>cakra</s> (wheel) of white radiance, (7)
with eight compartments filled with eight syllables,
having as its hub the initial [letter] of the practitioner's name placed in the center among the syllables oṃ and hā. (8)

children.text: dhyāyād ekāgracittaḥ san ṣaṇ māsān dṛḍhaniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should meditate with one-pointed mind for six months with firm resolve,

children.text: japed akhinnacittaḥ san mantram enaṃ daśākṣaram // Mvsts_9 //
children.translated_text: and recite with unwearied mind this ten-syllable <s>mantra</s>: (9)

children.text: oṅkāram ādito dattvā paścāt tāre prayojayet /
children.translated_text: Placing 'oṃ' at the beginning, then one should add '<s>tāre</s>,'

children.text: tuttāre syāt ture paścāt svāhāntaḥ sārvakarmikaḥ // Mvsts_10 //
children.translated_text: then '<s>tuttāre</s>,' then '<s>ture</s>,' ending with '<s>svāhā</s>' — [this mantra] is effective for all purposes. (10)

[The practitioner,] whose very hair-tips are undisturbed even by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Candra</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the Guardians of the Directions, and <s>Manmatha</s>,

children.text: apy akhaṇḍitaromāgro mṛtyuṃ jayati muktavat // Mvsts_11 //
children.translated_text: conquers death as if [already] liberated. (11)
[This practice brings] the destruction of wrinkles, grey hair, misfortune, disease, and poverty;
the elimination of the suffering and distress of the eight great fears beginning with lions. (12)
[It brings] unsolicited acquisition of garments, drinks, mansions, jewels, and the like;
the <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) of the sword, the eye-ointment, the foot-salve, the auspicious vase, and so forth. (13)
Poetry, eloquence, memory, and absolutely pure wisdom,

children.text: anyā ca vāñchitā siddhiś cakrād asmāt prajāyate // Mvsts_14 //
children.translated_text: and whatever other desired <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) — all arise from this <s>cakra</s>. (14)
This auspicious <s>sādhana</s> of <s>Sitatārā</s> (White Tārā) that destroys death and disease —

children.text: uddhṛtya yac chubhaṃ tena jagat tārā svayaṃ bhavet // Mvsts_15 //
children.translated_text: by whatever merit [comes from] extracting it, may the world itself be delivered by <s>Tārā</s>. (15)

body.translated_text: [End of] <s>Mṛtyuvañcanasitatārāsādhana</s> (The Sādhana of White Tārā for Cheating Death)
